title: Maximum Profit from a Single Stock Transaction with Day Gaps
statement_html:
You are given an integer array prices of length n, where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i, and an integer k.

You must make exactly one transaction: buy one share on some day i and sell it on a later day j (i < j). The profit is prices[j] - prices[i], which may be negative.

Return an array answer of length 4, where answer[c] is the maximum profit under condition c:

  1. answer[0]: the stock is sold any time after it is bought (j - i >= 1).

  2. answer[1]: sold exactly k days after it is bought (j - i == k).

  3. answer[2]: sold at least k days after it is bought (j - i >= k).

  4. answer[3]: sold at most k days after it is bought (1 <= j - i <= k).

Each case must be solved in O(n) time.

Example 1:

Input: prices = [7,1,5,3,6,4], k = 2
Output: [5,2,5,4]
Explanation:
- Any gap: buy at 1 (day 1), sell at 6 (day 4): 5.
- Gap exactly 2: buy at 1 (day 1), sell at 3 (day 3): 2.
- Gap at least 2: buy at 1 (day 1), sell at 6 (day 4), gap 3: 5.
- Gap at most 2: buy at 1 (day 1), sell at 5 (day 2): 4.

Example 2:

Input: prices = [9,7,4,3,1], k = 1
Output: [-1,-1,-1,-1]
Explanation: Prices only fall, so the best forced transaction loses 1 (e.g. buy at 4, sell at 3 the next day).

Example 3:

Input: prices = [3,8,2,9,1,6], k = 3
Output: [7,6,6,7]
Explanation:
- Any gap: buy at 2 (day 2), sell at 9 (day 3): 7.
- Gap exactly 3: buy at 3 (day 0), sell at 9 (day 3): 6.
- Gap at least 3: the same pair: 6.
- Gap at most 3: buy at 2 (day 2), sell at 9 (day 3): 7.

Constraints:

  • 2 <= n == prices.length <= 105

  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 109

  • 1 <= k <= n - 1

Similar to LeetCode #121. Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (differs in: exactly one transaction is forced, so profit can be negative, plus the exactly / at least / at most k day-gap conditions).
